items.q: Before phaeochromocytoma surgery, the essential first pharmacological step is what?
o: Alpha blockade with phenoxybenzamine plus volume expansion
items.exp: Irreversible alpha blockade and salt volume repletion tame catecholamine vasoconstriction over days. Beta blockade first leaves alpha unopposed and can precipitate crisis.
r: Incorrect. Beta first is the classic lethal sequence error.
Correct. Alpha blockade and volume first, always.
Incorrect. Embolisation is not standard preparation.
Incorrect. Steroids do not block catecholamine receptors.
items.kp: Phaeochromocytoma rule: alpha before beta, every time.

items.q: Tamsulosin improves prostatic symptoms with less hypotension mainly because it prefers which receptor?
items.exp: Alpha 1A receptors dominate prostate stroma and bladder neck, so uroselective blockade relaxes outflow with relatively spared vascular alpha 1B tone.
r: Incorrect. Alpha 2 is presynaptic and central mainly.
Correct. Alpha 1A selectivity targets the prostate.
Incorrect. Cardiac beta blockade does not relax prostate.
Incorrect. M3 blockade is antimuscarinic bladder therapy.
items.kp: Prostate flow drug equals alpha 1A selectivity.

items.q: First dose collapse after starting prazosin is best prevented how?
o: Low first dose taken at bedtime
items.exp: First dose postural hypotension follows sudden venodilation in a naive system; starting low at night and rising slowly minimises syncope risk.
r: Incorrect. Morning upright activity raises fall risk.
Correct. Low and at bedtime is the safe start.
Incorrect. Volume depletion worsens postural falls.
Incorrect. Rapid standing provokes the collapse.
items.kp: Start alpha blockers low, at night, rise slowly.

items.q: A cataract surgeon asks which drug history because of floppy iris syndrome. Which class?
items.exp: Alpha 1 blockade relaxes iris dilator muscle causing intraoperative floppy iris with billowing and prolapse, persisting long after stopping, so surgeons plan technique around the history.
r: Incorrect. Beta drops affect heart, not iris mechanics this way.
Correct. Tamsulosin class causes floppy iris.
Incorrect. Statins have no iris surgical syndrome.
Incorrect. Metformin matters for contrast, not iris tone.
items.kp: Floppy iris at surgery means alpha blocker history.

items.q: Phenoxybenzamine's blockade outlasts its plasma presence mainly because it binds how?
items.exp: Phenoxybenzamine alkylates alpha receptors permanently, so recovery awaits new receptor synthesis over days, suiting preoperative preparation that must not wear off mid surgery.
r: Incorrect. Phentolamine is the short competitive cousin.
Correct. Irreversible binding gives days of cover.
Incorrect. Duration is binding based, not metabolite based.
Incorrect. Store depletion describes reserpine or ephedrine fade.
items.kp: Irreversible phenoxybenzamine covers the whole operation.

items.q: Alpha blockers fell from first line hypertension mainly after trials showed excess what?
items.exp: The doxazosin arm of ALLHAT stopped early for more heart failure than chlorthalidone based therapy, demoting the class to add on status despite friendly metabolic effects.
r: Incorrect. Stroke rates were not the stopping signal.
Correct. Heart failure excess demoted the class.
Incorrect. Alpha blockers are metabolically neutral to friendly.
Incorrect. Gout belongs to diuretic adverse profiles.
items.kp: ALLHAT heart failure signal ended first line alpha use.

items.q: During phaeochromocytoma resection, a sudden hypertensive surge is best treated with which short alpha blocker?
items.exp: Phentolamine is rapid, short and reversible, ideal for intraoperative catecholamine surges alongside agents like nitroprusside or esmolol for rhythm. Oral long agents cannot titrate minute to minute.
r: Incorrect. Oral irreversible drug cannot rescue acute surges.
Correct. Intravenous phentolamine titrates surges.
Incorrect. Uroselective oral drug is far too slow and weak here.
Incorrect. Next day dosing misses the crisis entirely.
items.kp: Theatre surge in phaeo: phentolamine now.

items.q: Which counselling point is most specific to silodosin among prostate alpha blockers?
items.exp: Highly uroselective alpha blockade relaxes bladder neck closure during ejaculation, commonly causing retrograde or anejaculation that reverses on stopping and must be counselled before starting.
r: Incorrect. Hair effects belong to finasteride or minoxidil.
Correct. Ejaculatory change is the silodosin warning.
Incorrect. Gynecomastia follows spironolactone or finasteride more.
Incorrect. Blue vision is sildenafil PDE5 effect.
items.kp: Young man on silodosin: warn about ejaculation change.

items.q: Volume expansion accompanies phenoxybenzamine preparation chiefly because chronic vasoconstriction has caused what?
o: Contracted plasma volume with postural symptoms
items.exp: Years of catecholamine squeeze shrink effective circulating volume; when blockade vasodilates, unprepared patients collapse, so salt and fluids refill the tank before surgery.
r: Incorrect. Red cell mass is not the core issue.
Correct. The vascular tank is chronically underfilled.
Incorrect. Liver failure is unrelated to preparation logic.
Incorrect. Marrow effects are not part of this preparation.
items.kp: Block the squeeze, refill the tank.

items.q: Nonselective alpha blockade causes more reflex tachycardia than prazosin mainly because it also blocks which receptor?
items.exp: Alpha 2 blockade removes the brake on noradrenaline release, flooding beta 1 cardiac receptors. Selective alpha 1 drugs like prazosin spare feedback and calm the pulse response.
r: Incorrect. Alpha 1 blockade is shared by both types.
Correct. Losing alpha 2 feedback releases more transmitter.
Incorrect. Beta blockade would slow, not race, the heart.
Incorrect. Dopamine receptors are not the feedback brake here.
items.kp: Block the brake (alpha 2) and the heart races.
